coverage: Monday 10 Aug complete (Asia + US closes final). Plus a targeted check of the 3.5 hours since the US close — quiet, with one new Iran item. Asia opens ~1.5 hours after this was written.
tldr: ANSWERED DECISIVELY: Brent did not just hold Friday's $83.55 — it SETTLED $87.85, +5.15%, near the day's high with no fade. WTI settled $82.30 (+5.27%). The driver is the collapse of US-Iran Hormuz talks after Tehran escalated its reopening conditions.

OVERNIGHT: nothing reversed. Brent $87.72 (-0.15% off its settle), WTI $82.07, gold $4,397 (+0.14%), silver $65.74 — Monday's gains simply held. The one new item is Iran's parliament advancing a bill to charge tolls and restrict hostile-linked vessels in the strait; committee stage, not law, so read it as the hard line hardening rather than fresh escalation.

The honest nuance: deferred barrels led and the curve FLATTENED (Nov/Dec/Jan all ~+3.8% vs Oct +3.5%). That is the whole strip repricing, not acute prompt scarcity — a weaker signal than a front-led spike would be.

THE CROSS-CURRENT, NOW CONFIRMED AT THE CLOSE: the 10Y finished at 4.713% (+6.2bp) and the 30Y at 5.254% — its highest since 2007. A 5% crude day has rebuilt the September hike case that Friday's payrolls contraction tore down.

Silver closed $65.714 (+3.42%), gold $4,391.34 (+1.10%) — your largest position is ~+18% from late July. But GDX closed +0.67%, still trailing gold by ~43bp: the miners are participating at LESS than 1:1 beta, the opposite of the leverage they exist to provide.

Your HK sleeve: Xiaomi +2.07% (worth ~+HK$14,900 on your 26,662 units) behaving like a consumer stock, Tencent +0.54% defensive into Wednesday's results, SMIC -1.05% caught in the AI/memory de-rating. Hang Seng +1.05% but led by consumer/property/gold, NOT tech.
US equities finished fractionally red — S&P 7,753.11, just 4.53 points short of Friday's record, so the streak stopped one day short. Nasdaq -0.32%, Dow -0.11%.

regime.label: Oil breakout drives the hike case back
regime.oneLiner: Brent settled +5.15% on collapsed Hormuz talks, the 30Y hit its highest since 2007, and the September hike case is back three sessions after payrolls buried it.

topNews.headline: ANSWERED: Brent did NOT round-trip — it held $83.55 and broke out to ~$86.5 (+3.5%), a 4th straight up session
topNews.actionable: The Gulf premium is sticking rather than fading, which is the opposite of the last several geopolitical spikes — so Sunday's thesis was right on direction and Monday's early fade was the head-fake, not the signal. But read the flat curve honestly: this is the market repricing the whole strip, not panicking about prompt barrels. The second-order effect is the one that matters to you — crude +3.5% is reviving the inflation impulse that Friday's payrolls had just dismantled.

topNews.headline: 10Y yield climbs to a month high at 4.70% as oil revives inflation worry; September hike odds ~46%, down from ~64% a week ago
topNews.actionable: This is the cross-current. Oil at +3.5% has pushed the 10Y to a one-month high of 4.70%, rebuilding the September hike case that the payrolls contraction had dismantled three sessions ago. Your S-REITs and developers — which get their first mark tomorrow after the SGX holiday — face a higher discount rate than when they last traded.

topNews.headline: Silver hits a seven-week high at ~$65.1 spot (+2.5%) — the largest position in the book is working hard
topNews.actionable: Silver has run from ~$55.6 in late July to ~$65.1 — roughly +17%, and at 1.6x leverage that is a substantial gain on the IBKR equity. It is now rallying on the oil-driven inflation impulse, which is a different engine from last week's dovish-Fed rally. Note the tension: the same impulse that is lifting silver could revive the September hike that would hurt it.

topNews.headline: DIVERGENCE: GDX -0.14% while gold +0.41% near a two-month high and SILJ runs +2.09% — gold miners not confirming
topNews.actionable: Worth watching closely: the gold miners are NOT following gold today (GDX -0.14% against gold +0.41%) while the silver miners are (SILJ +2.09%). After GDX's 20%+ week that is either healthy consolidation or the first sign the miner rally has run ahead of the metal. Do not assume the sleeve moves as one.

topNews.headline: Hang Seng closed 25,937.49 (+1.05%); Hang Seng Tech 4,919 (+1.3%) — final closes
topNews.actionable: A clean +1.05% close on healthy HK$240bn turnover — but the gain came from consumer, property and precious-metals names, NOT tech. Do not read Hang Seng Tech +1.3% as broad tech strength; chips were negative underneath it.

topNews.headline: HK tech split on soft China CPI/PPI: Xiaomi +2.07%, Tencent +0.54%, SMIC -1.05% — all final closes
topNews.actionable: Xiaomi did the heavy lifting: +2.07% is worth roughly +HK$14,900 on your 26,662 units. It behaved like a consumer stock, which is exactly where the money rotated. SMIC (-1.05%) is the name exposed to the AI/memory de-rating spreading through Asian semis — that is the one to watch, not Tencent, which is trading defensively into Wednesday's results.

signals: Silver closed $65.714, ~+18% from late July on 1.6x leverage — but it is now an inflation-hedge trade, not a rate-cut trade. Wednesday's CPI is genuinely two-sided for it: a hot print feeds the impulse lifting silver AND revives the hike that would hurt it.

GDX +0.67% against gold +1.10% is the clearer warning now that it is a close, not an intraday print. Sub-1:1 beta on a strong gold day, after a 20%+ week, says the miner rally has run ahead of the metal.
The S-REIT sleeve reopens today against a 30Y at its highest since 2007. That is a bigger discount-rate problem than when it last traded on Friday — and it has one session before CPI.
SMIC is the HK name at risk — the AI/memory unwind took SK Hynix and Samsung negative on an up Korean day and knocked CSI AI -3% in the mainland. Tencent reports Wednesday.
Watch the ICE Brent settle tonight: a close above $85 would be the first genuine settle above the range top and would confirm the premium rather than the intraday spike.
